newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala's Arzu touts peace record in first year.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala's Arzu touts peace record in first year.

text.p: Basking in high public ratings and international acclaim for bringing peace to Guatemala after 36 years of civil war, President Alvaro Arzu touted his accomplishments on Tuesday in his annual report to congress.

"Few nations have the opportunity the Guatemalans have at this time ... the possibility of truly overcoming a tragic history of divisions and exclusions to find the correct way to peaceful co-existence," Arzu said.

A conservative businessman who took office one year ago, Arzu said his government brought the war with leftist rebels to an end by adopting a flexible negotiating position and attacking deep-rooted scepticism among Guatemalans. The government and leftist rebels of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit signed a historic peace treaty on Dec. 29.

A poll published on Tuesday in the country's largest circulation daily, Prensa Libre, showed about 43 percent of Guatemalans rated the government's first year in office as "good" and 18.5 percent rated it "very good" or "excellent."
A total of 278 Guatemalans took part in the telephone poll. No margin of error was given.

In his report Arzu acknowledged that economic growth in 1996 of 3.1 percent was not outstanding but pointed out that government spending had only increased 13 percent while tax collection was up 21 percent.
Arzu said he has rooted out corruption with an "intense purge of the executive branch" and straightened out the budget with a special temporary tax on income and the sale of government bonds.

He pronounced the army, once Guatemala's most powerful institution, firmly under civilian control saying "We can say with certainty and satisfaction that we can rely on an army that is subordinated to the established authorities."
